QF.id: Issue Management - General Obligations and Due Diligence_42

question.text: Which type of equity shares CANNOT be pledged even during the lock-in period?

answer.text: Ordinary equity shares held by promoters

explanation.text: The Logic: The pledge provision excludes Superior Voting Rights (SR) equity shares held by promoters and locked in. This category is carved out of the general pledge facility, while ordinary promoter shares can be pledged under specified conditions. The Trap: 'Ordinary equity shares held by promoters' can be pledged under specified conditions and so are not the correct answer. The SR-share carve-out is specific to SR equity shares held by promoters and under lock-in. Note: When reviewing a pledge proposal, segregate SR equity shares from ordinary promoter shares in the holding statement so the excluded category is not inadvertently pledged.
